chunks: What Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr —

He said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-Qadisiyyah — [when] I travel out to it, should I complete [the prayer] or shorten? He said: How far is it? I said: It is as you have seen. He said: Shorten.

key_terms.أُتِمُّ: complete — to perform the salat in its full (non-shortened) form as at home
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: shorten — to perform qasr salat, the shortened form obligatory for the traveler
key_terms.الْقَادِسِيَّةِ: al-Qadisiyyah — a town near Kufa (Iraq), the destination whose distance determines the prayer ruling
key_terms.قَصِّرْ: shorten! — the Imam's imperative legal ruling to perform qasr

ai.seo_question: Does traveling to al-Qadisiyyah meet the required distance for shortening (qasr) the prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal exchange between the narrator 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) concerning whether the salat should be performed in full or shortened (qasr) when traveling to al-Qadisiyyah, a town near Kufa in Iraq. The Imam inquires about the distance, receives the answer that it is as he had previously observed, and issues the definitive ruling: shorten — indicating that al-Qadisiyyah lies at or beyond the minimum travel distance (masafat al-qasr) that obligates abbreviated prayer.
